verdict.rationale: OpenClaw describes itself as a gateway connecting chat channels to AI coding agents. Its exec tool runs mutating shell commands that create and edit files in the workspace, and release notes mention repository-backed cloud work. A community report adds that it can use Claude Code as its harness via `claude -p`. However, no first-party doc shows supervising external coding agents end to end, and cloning and testing workflows are not documented. Missing for 10: first-party docs on embedding or supervising coding agents such as Claude Code or Codex, explicit repo clone/edit/test workflow, independent hands-on corroboration of repo work.

support.subject: As a developer, the assistant can supervise or embed real coding agents so it does repo work — cloning, editing, testing — not just snippets in chat

citations.quote: Self-hosted gateway that connects Discord, Google Chat, iMessage, Matrix, Microsoft Teams, Signal, Slack, Telegram, WhatsApp, Zalo, and more to AI coding agents.
`exec` is a mutating shell surface: commands can create, edit, or delete files wherever the selected host or sandbox filesystem permits.
OpenClaw used Claude Code as the harness via `claude -p`
